sources.citation: Kutsch Lojenga, Constance. 2003. Bila (D32). In D. Nurse & G. Philippson (eds.), The Bantu Languages, 450-474. London: Routledge. (publisher companion-site text layer held by the project; excerpt saved)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: a digital copy exists, behind a library sign-in
sources.note: Nothing on stress/accent anywhere in the chapter (a full-text search for stress/accent/prominence/penultimate = 0; 'accent' only names tone diacritics). On Kaiku specifically (p.450-452, fn.7): third variety of the Boone 1993 Bila survey, very little mutual intelligibility, ~80-81% lexical similarity with Bila, verbs end in -a not -o (possibly a 7-vowel system), k-loss (njoa 'snake', mbua 'seed'), uses nto/Gato 'person/people'; author treats it as a separate language. Bila prosody (sec. 2.3, pp.457-458) = three level tones H, L, extra-Low plus LH/xLH rising tones and downstep; tone only.
